repos/trade-imports-plants-frontend (DEFRA/trade-imports-plants-frontend, read on main at 2f2b07f, 27 November 2026) is the high-risk plants notification frontend: Node.js, Hapi, Nunjucks, GOV.UK Frontend 6.6.0 plus MOJ frontend and accessible-autocomplete, served on port 3003. It runs the same journey platform as the animals frontend: a journey-agnostic engine, bridge, model and services under src/server/app/ (out of this source's scope), with every piece of journey content in one set beneath it, src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/. This is a re-characterisation: the folder layout and file set are the same as at the last extract, but the code inside has moved since (among the commits since, the address-book pickers page at eight and name the chosen address, EUDPA-827, and a picker search by a country's name lists the addresses in that country, EUDPA-832), so every part is re-read in full. The scope takes in that set, src/server/app/shared/ (23 files, 2,828 lines: layout.njk, kit.js, save-actions.njk, section-caption.njk, error.njk, error-summary.njk, trail.js, set-context.js, paths.js, paging.js, render-macro.js, copy-leaves.js and the shared copy.en.js/copy.cy.js pair), the fit specs (22 files, 21 colocated with their feature and one, journey-smoke.fit.spec.js, in the repo-root fit/ folder, which also holds the 1,596-line high-risk-plants-journey.js harness, set-base.js, sign-in.js and seed-fields.js, 1,965 lines in all), and the set's own decisions and rulings ledgers. Inside the set: journeys/linear/features/ holds 19 feature folders (dashboard, hub, commodity-type, commodities, origin, arrival-status, arrival-details, consignor-select, identification-numbers, consignment-contact-select, place-of-destination, party-edit, address-book-picker, check-answers, review, declaration, confirmation, delete-notification, cancel-amend, plus the cross-page fit specs and index.js beside them), each with page.js, controller.js, an optional template.njk, fields.js where it collects, a copy/copy.en.js and copy/copy.cy.js pair, a view-model/ folder where it needs one, a <name>.fit.spec.js and unit tests; journeys/linear/flow/ holds flow.js (five sections: start, about-the-consignment, arrival-and-destination, consignment-parties and a review section behind a readyForCheckYourAnswers gate), task-rows.js (seven hub rows), entry-guard.js, section-captions/ and a 362-line happy-path fixture; journeys/linear/parties/ (91 lines) holds the picked-party rules; obligations/ (816 lines) holds the obligation manifest index.js and seven section files (origin, arrival, parties, destination, commodity, contact, review); services/commodities/ (517 lines) holds the set-owned commodity vocabulary; spec/ holds the ledgers - journey-spec.json (2,814 lines), decisions.json (97 decisions, 1,654 lines), conflicts.json (40 conflicts, 423 lines), backlog-extras.json (557 lines) and panel/ (rulings.json with 8 dockets and 83 rulings in 3,008 lines, critic.json 183 lines, README.md); docs/ (13 markdown files, 3,128 lines: README.md's served-surface reference, obligation-model.md, features.md, journey-flow-and-gates.md, services.md, limits.md, testing.md, copy-status.md, lighthouse.md and four add-a-* recipes). The served surface is a notification list at /, a task-list hub at /notifications/{journeyId}, the collecting pages commodity-type, commodities and commodities/details, origin, arrival-status, arrival-details, destinations/select, consignors/select, identification-numbers and consignment/contact/select, a review section of notification-view, declaration and confirmation, the action slugs amend, cancel-amend, copy and delete, and a party-edit page reached from a picked address. Scope leaves out the generic engine, bridge, model, analysis, page-maturity and services folders under src/server/app/ (including the persistence, address-book, countries and ports clients), and everything under src/auth, src/config, src/plugins, src/client, src/shared, test/, tests/ and eslint-rules/; five files outside the scoped folders are read narrowly because the set depends on them: src/server/app/routes-high-risk-plants.js, src/server/app/routes.js, src/server/router.js and src/server/app/bridge/fulfilment-registry.js for where the set's routes mount (part 12), and src/server/common/components/submitted-search/macro.njk for the picker's search box (part 9). The parts below cut the scope by what a user sees - a group of pages at a time - with the route registration and obligation manifest, the shared kit, the fit harness, each ledger and the set docs as parts of their own. Unit tests (*.test.js) sit inside the folders the parts name and are read for the behaviour and copy they pin down; the fit specs are claimed in their own right because the scope names them.

Extracted in 18 parts:
Part 1, Notification list and its row actions: Part 1 read the dashboard feature folder of the high-risk plants set in full, at main 2f2b07f: page.js (the page descriptor, slug '' and maturity exploring), controller.js (four routes: GET / for the list, POST /notifications/{journeyId}/amend, POST /notifications to start a draft and GET /start, the front-door entry), template.njk (banners, caption, H1, intro, guidance link, start button, the search panel in a third column and the results column holding the results line, the sort form, one GOV.UK summary card per notification, the empty state and Previous/Next pagination), notification-helper.js (sort values and default, date and commodity formatting, page clamping, list query string, pagination links and results range wording), view-model/row/index.js (one card's cells), view-model/row/actions.js (the actions per status: draft, submitted, amend, anything else), view-model/sort-options.js, the copy pair copy/copy.en.js and copy/copy.cy.js, and the unit tests controller.test.js, notification-helper.test.js, late-tag.test.js, view-model/row/index.test.js and copy/copy.test.js, plus the 16 Playwright fit tests of dashboard.fit.spec.js. It also read flow/notification-action-slugs.js (amend, cancel-amend, copy, delete). It read shared/kit.js, shared/paging.js, shared/layout.njk and review/lateness.js for context only. Since the last extract (a88175f) the folder changed only in one test helper line (controller.test.js now submits rather than finalises a seeded notification) and kit.js gained an import block, which moved its line numbers; every earlier claim was re-checked against the code and kept, four with their kit.js line refs updated. It covers the list page at the set root with all its copy in English and Welsh, the status and Late tags, every row action with its href or post target and the states it appears for, the create and start entries with their logging, the amend post with its refusal banner, paging, sorting and search, and what the fit tests and unit tests prove or leave unproven.
Part 2, Task-list hub, journey flow, task rows, section captions and the entry guard: Part 2 read, in full on main at 2f2b07f: the hub feature folder (page.js, controller.js, template.njk, hub.fit.spec.js with its 10 tests, controller.test.js, copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js, copy/copy.test.js); flow/flow.js and flow.test.js; flow/task-rows.js and task-rows.test.js; flow/entry-guard.js and entry-guard.test.js; flow/navigation.test.js; flow/save-and-continue.test.js; flow/section-captions/ (index.js, section-captions.test.js and its copy pair and copy test); flow/fixtures/happy-path.json (five cases); journeys/linear/config.js; journeys/linear/test-support.js; and, for context only, shared/save-actions.njk and shared/section-caption.njk. It covers the Overview hub at /high-risk-plants/notifications/{journeyId} (H1, task-list heading, four numbered groups, the seven task rows plus the review row built from the review section, every status and the rule behind it, Back and Return to dashboard), the five flow sections and their pages with the readyForCheckYourAnswers gate, FLOW_ONLY_KEYS (declaration only), the entry guard (what it guards and exempts, the started test, the redirect to commodity type, its log line and its new journey.entry.redirect metric), the five section captions and the bare pages, Save and continue order and fallbacks for plants or wood and for potatoes, the Back and Cancel rules test-support pins, and the happy-path fixture. Since the last extract only entry-guard.js and its test changed (a redirect metric, shifting their line numbers); every other file is unchanged. Kept ids 001-134 hold the same claims with entry-guard refs renumbered; 135-140 are new.
Part 3, Commodity type and the set-owned commodity vocabulary: Part 3 read, on main at 2f2b07f, every file of journeys/linear/features/commodity-type/ in full (page.js 5 lines, evaluation.js 9, controller.js 151, template.njk 38, controller.test.js 418, commodity-type.fit.spec.js 349 with 17 tests, copy/copy.en.js 36, copy/copy.cy.js 31, copy/copy.test.js 90) and services/commodities/ in full (index.js 290, commodities.test.js 227). For context only, it read flow/flow.js (commodity-type is the first page of the about-the-consignment section, after the dashboard's start section), flow/entry-guard.js, features/timing-windows.js, features/commodities/links.js, obligations/sections/commodity.js, arrival.js and parties.js, the shared journey test-support.js, and the parts of shared/kit.js the page calls (base, nextTarget, recoverableSave, pageRoutes and its stale-action wrapper). The slice is one page: the commodity-type question at /high-risk-plants/notifications/{journeyId}/commodity-type, a single required radio group of three types with timing hints, a lines-removal warning, the three shared save controls, its back and cancel destinations, its refusals, its type-change line purge and its save failure; then the set-owned commodity vocabulary the page and the commodity pages read (3 commodity types, 9 categories partitioned by type, 15 genus entries with a 3-entry hardwood list, 3 origin constraints narrowest first, 9 per-line fields with the categories each applies to). Claims cover the route, entry guard, heading, caption, hint, every option label and hint, every English and Welsh copy key, the error, every branch (the commodities list, the overview, the removal report, and the potato versus plants-and-wood fork in arrival and parties scope), every unit and fit test, the vocabulary as hard-coded data whose owner (V4 or MDM through reference-data) is an open question, and evaluation.js as a mechanism. It stops at the commodities list and details pages, which part 4 claims.
Part 4, Commodity lines: the list page and the details sub-page: Part 4 read the commodities feature folder of the high-risk plants linear journey in full (src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/journeys/linear/features/commodities/: page.js, fields.js, evaluation.js, entry-index.js, links.js, line-form.js, list/list.controller.js, list/list.njk, list/_cells.njk, list/table-rows.js, details/details.controller.js, details/details.njk, copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js, and the unit tests list.controller.test.js, details.controller.test.js, table-rows.test.js and copy.test.js), plus as context only services/commodities/index.js (part 3), obligations/sections/commodity.js (part 12) and shared/kit.js (part 13). It covers two pages. The commodities list page (slug 'commodities', GET and POST at /notifications/{journeyId}/commodities) owns the commodityLines collection: a four-column table (Category, Genus or variety, Quantity, hidden Actions) with a Change link and a Remove button per row, an empty state, the 'Add another commodity' button, the removal banner after a commodity-type change, the 'Add at least one commodity' collection floor, no ceiling, and Save and continue alone. The commodity details sub-page (slug 'commodities/details', ?index=N to edit) asks the category radios first, then reveals the per-line fields that category asks for (genus type-ahead, species, commodity code, variety, quantity, intended use, EPPO code, size of the trees, phytosanitary treatments) with their labels, hints, widths, caps and verbatim errors, and saves by Save and continue or Save and add another. Claims also cover the guards on a forged or stale index, the trail-carrying redirects, save failures, the English and Welsh copy bundles key by key, the 12 tests of fit/list.fit.spec.js and the 18 of fit/details.fit.spec.js one claim each, and the four mechanism modules. The repo has moved since the earlier extract only in two test helper renames and in kit.js's save-fallback logging, so every kept claim still says the same thing.
Part 5, Origin and arrival status: Part 5, Origin and arrival status. Read in full, at repo HEAD 2f2b07f: every file of journeys/linear/features/origin/ (evaluation.js, page.js, controller.js, template.njk, controller.test.js, origin.fit.spec.js, copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js, copy/copy.test.js) and every file of journeys/linear/features/arrival-status/ (evaluation.js, page.js, controller.js, template.njk, statuses.js, controller.test.js, arrival-status.fit.spec.js, copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js, copy/copy.test.js), plus obligations/sections/origin.js, obligations/sections/arrival.js and shared/kit.js for context only (parts 12 and 13 claim them). Since the earlier extract (a88175f) only the two controller tests' backend-failure helper and kit.js's stale-concurrency and save-fallback logging changed; no page, copy or rule in this slice moved. Covered: the origin page (route, heading, caption, the one country type-ahead over a native select and its configuration, select text, placeholder, no-results text, required and membership rule, the three per-category narrowing rules and their messages, territory-to-parent-country matching, the ware-potato guidance inset, the stale saved country state, save controls, Back link, redirects, save failures); the arrival-status page (route, legend as h1, caption, the two statuses with labels and hints, the 4-day window in the post-arrival hint, the required rule, Save and return refusals, redirects, save failures); the scope rule that skips arrival status for potatoes and what a potato notifier sees instead; every English and Welsh copy key in both features; all 19 tests of origin.fit.spec.js and all 18 of arrival-status.fit.spec.js; both evaluation.js bindings as mechanism claims.
Part 6, Arrival details: Part 6, Arrival details. Read in full every file of src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/journeys/linear/features/arrival-details/: page.js (slug and maturity), controller.js (GET and POST handlers, the date state chosen from commodity scope and arrival status, the date, time and place-of-landing rules, the stale-port check, the recoverable save), fields.js (the three field names and the three date states), template.njk (MoJ date picker, GOV.UK time input, accessible-autocomplete place of landing, save actions), arrival-bounds.js and its test (the today cap in Europe/London), evaluation.js (the three scalar bindings), copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js and copy/copy.test.js, controller.test.js and arrival-details.fit.spec.js (26 own tests plus the four describeDatePickerLook adds). One page covered: arrival-details at /high-risk-plants/notifications/{journeyId}/arrival-details, asked in three wordings (potatoes, not yet arrived, already arrived), with time and place of landing for potatoes only. Since the earlier extract the slice's code is unchanged; only a test helper name in controller.test.js and kit.js's stale-refusal and logging internals moved, so every earlier claim is kept, two kit line references are updated and one claim on the save-fallback log is added.
Part 7, Consignor picker, identification numbers and consignment contact picker: Part 7 read, in full, three feature folders of the high-risk plants linear journey and its parties registry, at repo HEAD 2f2b07fd. consignor-select/ (page.js, fields.js, evaluation.js, controller.js, controller.test.js, consignor-select.fit.spec.js with 10 own tests, copy en/cy/test, view-model index and test) is a thin binding of the shared address-book picker shell at slug consignors/select, role CONSIGNOR, scoped by the consignor obligation. identification-numbers/ (page.js, fields.js, evaluation.js, controller.js, template.njk, controller.test.js, identification-numbers.fit.spec.js with 6 test declarations, three of them looped per commodity type, copy en/cy/test) is a hand-built form of four text inputs, each shown by its own obligation's scope, max 58 characters. consignment-contact-select/ (page.js, fields.js, evaluation.js, controller.js, controller.test.js, consignment-contact-select.fit.spec.js with 11 own tests, copy en/cy/test, view-model index and test) binds the same picker shell at consignment/contact/select with no role and its own return-control words. parties/ (index.js, picked-party.js, picked-party.test.js) registers the three copied-address answers and the copy-on-pick and display rules. Read in full every file of features/place-of-destination/ (evaluation.js, page.js, fields.js, controller.js, controller.test.js, place-of-destination.fit.spec.js, copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js, copy/copy.test.js, view-model/index.js, view-model/view-model.test.js) and of features/party-edit/ (page.js, party-edit.controller.js, party-edit.controller.test.js, party-edit.njk, party-edit.fit.spec.js, edit-href.js, address-rules.js, address-rules.test.js, copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js, copy/copy.test.js). Part 9, The address book picker shell: Part 9, the address book picker shell: the feature folder src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/journeys/linear/features/address-book-picker/, read in full (all 22 files: picker-routes.js, render.js, view-model.js, table-rows.js and its test, address-lines.js and its test, pagination.js, results-href.js, results.njk and its test, template.njk, _cells.njk, held-copy.njk, save-selection.js and its test, test-support.js, controller-test-support.js, paging-test-support.js, copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js, copy/copy.test.js), with src/server/common/components/submitted-search/macro.njk for the search box, and src/server/app/shared/paging.js and kit.js as context only (part 13 claims them). The picker pages' own headings, descriptions, titles and error wording belong to parts 7 and 8.
Part 10, Check your answers and the review helpers: Part 10, check your answers and the review helpers. Read in full: every file of features/check-answers (page.js, controller.js, controller.test.js, template.njk, refusal.js, check-answers.fit.spec.js, copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js, copy/copy.test.js, view-model/index.js, view-header.js, view-header.test.js, incomplete-cards.js, incomplete-cards.test.js, invalid-parties.js and the four rows/ helpers) and every file of features/review (evaluation.js, lateness.js, lateness.test.js, late-rule.js, late-rule.test.js, notification-day-text.js, notification-day-text.test.js). For an amendment it is a 'Check your answers' review with the journey strip. Below that sit three numbered sections of summary cards (Import details, Commodity N, Arrival details, place of destination, Consignor, Identification numbers, Contact). Then come the outstanding-card and party-address errors, the late warning for a draft and the late banner for a submitted notification, the amendment-cancelled banner, and the submit form with Continue, the shared save actions and Cancel amend. The slice has not changed since the earlier extract's commit (a88175f), so every kept claim still says the same thing, and claims 175 to 177 add what that extract left out. obligations/sections/review.js and shared/kit.js were read for context only: parts 12 and 13 claim them.
Part 11, Declaration, confirmation, delete notification and cancel amend: Part 11, the high-risk plants journey's endings, read in full: the four feature folders under src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/journeys/linear/features/ named declaration (page.js, controller.js, controller.test.js, template.njk, declaration.fit.spec.js, copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js, copy/copy.test.js), confirmation (the same eight files), delete-notification (the same eight files) and cancel-amend (the same eight files, its page.js carrying id but no slug), plus src/server/app/shared/kit.js for context only (part 13 claims it; read at lines 78-110, 256-281 and 330-363 to resolve the slugs, the status strip, the caption and the stale-change guard the slice's controllers use) and src/server/app/shared/copy.en.js's notificationActions.delete block (lines 55-59) for the delete success banner the slice's fit spec asserts. review/lateness.js is named for context only and part 10 claims it; the slice records only how the declaration calls it. Part 14, The fit harness and the journey smoke spec: Part 14 read the repo-root fit folder's journey smoke spec and its harness in full: fit/journey-smoke.fit.spec.js (225 lines), fit/high-risk-plants-journey.js (1596 lines), fit/set-base.js (125), fit/sign-in.js (9) and fit/seed-fields.js (10), plus the copy modules and the happy-path fixture they import, only to resolve the words and steps the specs assert. The smoke spec declares 4 tests: (1) a loop over the five happy-path shapes, each walked from the dashboard to confirmation with the trail asserted on every step, the draft review checked, the declaration submitted, the confirmation heading, reference and late heading asserted, and axe run; (2) a loop over the ware-potato and wood shapes proving Back on the commodities list, arrival details, identification numbers and contact opens the step Save and continue came from; (3) Back then Save and continue carries on to the next step; (4) Back twice from arrival details reaches origin then the commodities list. The harness holds the potato walk in order (commodity type, commodity details, commodities list, origin, arrival details, place of destination, identification numbers, consignment contact, review, declaration, confirmation), the wood walk's branch through arrival status, the draft-review, declaration and confirmation helpers, the three save controls, the type-ahead and calendar helpers, the axe check, and the shared address-picker suites (listing, search, paging, row lines and disclosure, saving, refusing an id not in the book). Branches covered: by commodity type (potatoes vs plants and wood: arrival status and consignor asked only for the latter; identification numbers differ), by arrival status and lateness. Amend and copy are not walked here (a gap). set-base.js, sign-in.js and seed-fields.js are claimed as mechanisms: URL matchers anchored on the /high-risk-plants mount and the application's own trail encoding, stub sign-in as organisation stub-org-1, and relative arrival dates. The files are unchanged since the earlier extract's commit, so every earlier p14 claim and p11-037 is kept; three new claims add the plants and wood walk order, the trail-less direct page address and the late after-arrival case.
Part 15, The set's journey specification: Part 15 read src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/spec/journey-spec.json (2814 lines) and spec/fixtures/happy-path.json (one line). The specification has seven top-level keys: specVersion 1; journey high-risk-plants-import-notification; 7 sources (policy paper, Confluence user needs, Confluence requirements, mural, design prototype, live animals frontend, skeleton); 98 behaviours, each with id, source, status, detail and an optional ruling decision; one fieldGroup (address); 8 sections (start, commodity, origin, arrival, destination, parties, contact, review) with a gate, title and pages, each page with its pattern, caption, route, collects and notes; and 29 obligations, each with its level (appliesAt), kind, mandate, input widget, values and format, label, hint, error copy, enforcement at continue, animals relation and ruled notes. The happy-path fixture is one line, schema_version 1 with an empty values object. Claims run in file order: sources, behaviours, sections and pages, the address field group, obligations, then the fixture, plus inferred and gap claims where the specification and the pages disagree or the specification states something no page implements. claims.statement: A line index asked for in a link or posted in a form is acted on only when it is a whole number the collection actually holds; anything else is treated as naming no line.
claims.note: mechanism: validates the `index` query parameter or form field of a commodity line before a render or a write sees it.

claims.statement: Every link and redirect between the list page, the details page and the commodity-type question keeps the trail of pages the trader walked, so Back and the eventual return always point at the page they actually came from.
claims.quote:
const hrefWith = (request, slug, entries) =>
  kit.carryTrail(request, pathWith(request.params.journeyId, slug, entries))
claims.note: mechanism: builds the commodity pages' own hrefs — the list, the details page with or without an index, and the commodity-type question with the newest place dropped — from the journey id and the request's trail.

claims.statement: After a change of commodity type has dropped lines, the trader is sent to the list page with the number dropped in the address and the commodity-type question added to the trail.
claims.quote:
export const listHrefAfterTypeChange = (request, removed) =>
  kit.pushTrail(
    request,
    pathWith(request.params.journeyId, commoditiesPage.slug, [
      ['removed', String(removed)]
    ]),
    commodityTypePage.slug
  )
claims.note: mechanism: turns a count of dropped commodity lines into the list page's `removed` query parameter. The commodity-type page that calls it is part 3's.

claims.statement: Each per-line field is rendered as the kind and width of control its own name decides: the genus as a select, phytosanitary treatments as a textarea, and everything else as a text input, with set widths and a numeric keypad for the quantity.
claims.note: mechanism: maps a commodity-line field name to its widget, GOV.UK width class, inputmode and character cap, read by the details page's view model.

claims.statement: The commodities table a trader sees is built row by row from the saved lines, each row's fourth cell holding the Change link and Remove button for that line.
claims.note: mechanism: turns the controller's commodity rows into GOV.UK table cells, rendering the actions cell through the feature's own Nunjucks macro. With no line it returns no rows.

claims.statement: Which per-line answers count towards a notification being complete is decided per line and per category: each field is in scope only on the categories that ask for it, and the quantity on every line.
claims.quote:
const lineLeaf = (field, obligation) =>
  grouped({ field, obligation, groups: [line] })
claims.note: mechanism: binds the ten per-line answer names (category, genus, species, commodityCode, quantity, potatoVariety, potatoIntendedUse, eppoCode, sizeOfTree, phytosanitaryTreatments) to their obligations within the commodityLines group. The manifest and the engine are other parts'.

claims.statement: The commodity pages hold no character-count countdown, no 'you have N characters remaining' message and no other JavaScript enhancement beyond the genus type-ahead.
claims.quote: {% from "accessible-autocomplete/macro.njk" import appAccessibleAutocomplete %}
claims.note: It follows because the only enhanced control either template imports is the accessible-autocomplete macro: the 400-character treatments answer uses govukTextarea with no maxlength or character count, and every other field is a plain govukInput.

claims.statement: A backend that cannot take a line's save on the details page is logged once at warn as a save fallback with the journey id and route, but, unlike a removal on the list page, without naming an action or the line's index.
claims.note: It follows because the details page passes no ids argument to recoverableSave, while the list page passes { action: 'remove-line', index }. kit.js itself is part 13's. No test pins the details page's log line.

claims.statement: Every request to the set is checked by the journey entry guard before the page runs, and a request that fails it is redirected away rather than served.
The set refuses to start if any of its configuration seams is unfilled or any of its journey cookies is unregistered, so a misconfigured journey fails at boot rather than serving half a journey.

claims.statement: The notifier says whether the consignment has arrived rather than the service working it out from the arrival date, because one branch of the rules turns on arrival in the country and the other on arrival at the destination, and a date alone cannot tell them apart.

* The notifier says so rather than the service deriving it from the arrival
 * date: reg 26(2)(a) branches on arrival in the country and reg 26(2)(b) on
 * arrival at the intended destination, and a date alone cannot say which
 * branch a consignment arriving today is in.

claims.statement: Pages are server-rendered by preference, and the only client-side code in the journey is the accessible autocomplete on the origin, arrival details and commodity details pages.
claims.quote: Prefer server-rendered controls. When a page genuinely needs a client bundle (the accessible-autocomplete on origin, arrival-details and commodity-details already ships as a common component; any add-another or conditional-reveal enhancement beyond govuk radios)

claims.statement: Every page is audited by Lighthouse after signing in, with floors of 0.60 for performance and 0.70 for accessibility and best practices, and no search-engine assertion is to be added.
claims.quote: desktop preset, signing in first through the Defra ID stub, score floors performance 0.60 / accessibility 0.70 / best-practices 0.70 and NO SEO assertion (none should be added)

claims.statement: A trader can change any answer before submitting, through save and return, the overview statuses, inline validation and a Change link on every check your answers row; the policy paper says nothing about amending after submission.
claims.quote: The paper says nothing about amendment after submission — that is notification-actions-after-submission (open question, c-030).

claims.statement: The journey has no payment step, fee display or invoice reference anywhere, because the decision was taken not to charge for these activities.
claims.quote: There is no payment step, fee display or invoice reference anywhere in the journey.

claims.statement: The journey must not ask for, require or upload an export certificate, a phytosanitary certificate or any other document, so it has no documents collection, no upload page and no document references.
claims.quote: The journey must not ask for, require or upload an export certificate, phytosanitary certificate or any other document — no documents collection, no upload page, no document references.

claims.statement: The notification is not matched to a customs declaration and holds no goods, so the journey collects no customs reference and no transport or port of exit details.
claims.quote: the journey collects no customs reference (MRN, entry number) and no transport or port-of-exit details — none of animals' transport section is copied

claims.statement: Plant passports stay a separate regime: the notification neither asks for, uploads nor replaces passport data, and the supplier identification number and EPPO code are typed in rather than read from a document.
claims.quote: Plant passports are a separate regime: the notification does not ask for, upload or replace passport data.

claims.statement: The journey's order follows what is arriving, when and where: commodity, then origin, then arrival, then destination, then parties, then contact, then review, and the category, genus, origin, destination and date are coded or structured rather than free text so inspectors can decide where to spot check.
claims.quote: are the spine of the journey and the section order: commodity (what) -> origin (where from) -> arrival (when) -> destination (where to) -> parties -> contact -> review

claims.statement: A notification carries exactly one commodity type, chosen first, so a mixed consignment needs two notifications, and the commodity type page's hint says so.
claims.quote: A notification therefore carries exactly one commodityType chosen first; a mixed consignment is two notifications. The commodity-type hint says so.

claims.statement: A question outside the consignment's scope is neither shown, validated nor saved, and a page whose every question is out of scope is skipped, so the trader is asked only what their consignment needs.
claims.quote: out-of-scope fields are neither rendered nor validated nor committed, arrival-status is skipped for potatoes, and the derived gates hide a page whose every obligation is out of scope

claims.statement: The digital submission is the written notification to the authority, attributed to the signed-in organisation and user, kept as a submitted record with a unique reference, a date of notification and the declaration, and no separate notifier identity is typed in.
claims.quote: The signed-in organisation is the professional operator; no separate notifier identity is typed (c-038).

claims.statement: Back on every journey page and on check your answers returns to where the trader came from, the place travelling on the link or form rather than being held in the session, with the entry page going back to the overview once answers exist and to the dashboard otherwise, the declaration going back to check your answers and the confirmation having no back link.
claims.quote: The entry page (commodity-type) goes Back to the Overview when the notification already has committed answers and to the dashboard otherwise.

claims.statement: The trail of places Back can return to keeps the newest forty, past which the oldest drop and Back ends at the overview.
claims.quote: the trail keeps the newest 40 places, past which the oldest drop and Back ends at the Overview

claims.statement: The trace chain for an outbreak is the consignor, the supplier, producer and crop identification numbers, the country of origin and the place of destination or current location, all captured as required matters with nothing extra asked, and the identifiers stored exactly as entered.
claims.quote: The consignor, supplier identification number, producer and crop identification numbers, country of origin and place of destination / current location are the trace chain and are all captured as required matters; nothing extra is asked.

claims.statement: A late or post-arrival notification is accepted and recorded rather than blocked: the arrival date has no future-only rule, the declaration submits whatever the timing, and lateness is recorded as a flag shown to the notifier and the authority.
claims.quote: A late or post-arrival notification is therefore ACCEPTED and recorded, never blocked: arrivalDate has no future-only rule, the declaration submits regardless of timing, and lateness is a flag (lateNotificationIndicator) shown to the notifier and the authority.

claims.statement: Five journeys are the service's worked examples and test fixtures: ware potatoes from Spain or Poland, ware potatoes notified late, seed potatoes from any EU country, spruce from any EU country, and conifer wood from Italy, France, Portugal or Spain.
claims.quote: Ware potatoes from Spain/Poland; Ware potatoes from Spain/Portugal with a late notification; Seed potatoes from any EU country; Spruce (Picea) from any EU country; Conifer wood from Italy, France, Portugal or Spain

claims.statement: A single-question radios page uses its legend as the page heading with the section caption above it, a single-input page uses a heading with the field label as the heading, and an address picker keeps a heading plus a description.
claims.quote: a single-question radios page (commodity-type, arrival-status) uses the legend as the page heading with the section caption above it; a single-input page uses an h1 with the label as the heading; the address pickers keep animals' h1 + description.

claims.statement: The journey is built from GOV.UK Frontend 6.x and Ministry of Justice Frontend 11.x components and utility classes only, with no hand-rolled components and no custom CSS, and the animals service's bespoke classes and totals panel are not copied.
claims.quote: no hand-rolled components or custom CSS. Animals' bespoke classes (app-commodity-total*, notification-list__*, app-link-button, app-form-inline) and its custom hub totals panel are debt and are not copied

claims.statement: The plants journey asks no reason for import and no purpose question, so it uses none of the import reason and purpose, transport reference or commercial transporter services the platform carries.
claims.quote: No plants source asks a reason-for-import or purpose question — the potato 'intended use' and the optional 'use' are free-text per-line matters — so the plants journey does not use this service and the platform's transport-reference and commercial-transporters services are likewise unused.

claims.statement: Guidance is published outside the service: the journey has no separate guidance or before-you-start pages, and meets the trader's need to understand the scheme through the dashboard introduction, a GOV.UK guidance link, the commodity type option hints and per-field hints.
claims.quote: are met inside the journey by the dashboard intro copy, a GOV.UK guidance link, the commodity-type option hints (timing windows) and per-field hint text, not by separate guidance or before-you-start pages

claims.statement: A potato notification must be made at least two days before the expected arrival and a plants or wood notification before arrival or no later than four days after it, and a notification outside its window is flagged as late.
claims.quote: potatoes: late if submitted after arrivalDate minus 2 days; plants/wood: late if submitted more than 4 days after arrivalDate; a future date is never late

claims.statement: Lateness is worked out once, in London time, on calendar days ignoring the arrival time, stored on the record at the first submission and read back by the confirmation, the submitted view and the notification list rather than recomputed.
claims.quote: calendar-day rule per c-031 (potatoes late after arrivalDate minus 2, plants and wood late after arrivalDate plus 4; arrivalTime ignored; a future date is never late for plants and wood)

claims.statement: The trader says whether the consignment has arrived rather than the service working it out from the date, with Yes offered first, and the question is asked before the arrival details and the destination.
claims.quote: Build the user-selected arrivalStatus radios page (Yes first) for plants and wood, placed before arrival-details and place-of-destination; potatoes have no status and Save and continue passes over the page by the derived gate. The service never derives the status from the date.

claims.statement: Every string the notifier reads says Great Britain, and no nation check is applied to the destination address, so Scottish and Welsh destinations are notified through this service.
claims.quote: Great Britain in all notifier-facing copy; no nation check on placeOfDestination; Scottish and Welsh destinations notify through this service.

claims.statement: The origin page refuses a country outside the lists allowed for the categories on the notification, naming the allowed countries in the error, and check your answers re-checks the same rule and refuses to continue with a Change link to the origin page.
claims.quote: an out-of-scope origin is rejected with the narrowingErrorCopy sentence naming the allowed countries; Balearic inset (potato-scope-guidance, c-021) when a ware-potatoes line exists; notification-view re-checks and refuses POST with a Change link to origin.

claims.statement: The allowed origins are Poland, Portugal, Romania or Spain for ware potatoes, Italy, France, Portugal or Spain for conifer wood without bark, any EU member state for plants and other wood, and any primed country for seed potatoes, with the effective list the intersection of those for the categories present.
claims.quote: effective list = intersection of the per-category lists for the categories present in commodityLines (ware-potatoes PL/PT/RO/ES; conifer-wood-without-bark IT/FR/PT/ES; plants and other wood EU_MEMBER_STATES; seed-potatoes ANY_PRIMED_COUNTRY)

claims.statement: Changing the commodity type keeps the lines whose category belongs to the new type and drops the rest, warning before the change while lines exist and reporting the number removed in a banner on the commodities list, whichever save control was pressed.
claims.quote: keep lines whose category is in the new type's set, drop the rest with wipe semantics), the page warns before when lines exist, and it redirects to the commodities list with ?removed=<n> carrying where the trader came from, whichever save control was pressed

claims.statement: The arrival date is any real calendar date with no sanity window and no picker limits, except that an already-arrived consignment cannot be dated in the future, and a past expected date for potatoes is accepted and simply shows up as late.
claims.quote: Build arrivalDate as a real calendar date with no sanity window and no picker min/max, except a maximum of today when arrivalStatus = already-arrived, from one bounds helper beside arrival-details.

claims.statement: The notification reference is shown exactly as the backend mints it, a two-digit year and six characters with no type-code prefix, because the plants type code has not been decided, and the frontend never validates or parses it.
claims.quote: The frontend never validates or parses the reference, so the journey builds on the unprefixed backend format shown verbatim

claims.statement: A notification's status is one of draft, submitted, being amended or deleted, all four reachable, shown as the tags Draft, Submitted, Amending and Deleted, and lateness is never a status value but a separate tag and banner.
claims.quote: the dashboard tag and journey strip read Draft / Submitted / Amending / Deleted and all four are reachable in the first pass (Amend is in scope, c-030); the Late tag on the dashboard card and the banners are the lateNotificationIndicator rendering, never a status value

claims.statement: The notification list offers View, Amend and Delete on a submitted notification, Resume and Delete on a draft, and Resume, Cancel amendment and Delete while amending, and the read-only view offers Delete when submitted and a Cancel amendment link while amending, with no Copy as new anywhere.
claims.quote: dashboard SUBMITTED: View | Amend | Delete; DRAFT: Resume | Delete; AMEND: Resume | Cancel amendment | Delete; CYA read-only offers Delete (SUBMITTED) and the Cancel amendment link (AMEND)

claims.statement: The service's name, feedback address, helpdesk contact lines and the homes of the Address book and Manage account links are undecided, so the inherited chrome ships as it is and the help text names the relevant plant health authority with no contact lines.
claims.quote: the shared chrome ships verbatim; the confirmation help block names the relevant plant health authority (APHA, the Forestry Commission or Scottish Government) with no contact lines and carries provisionalCopy

claims.statement: The country list comes from reference data's SPS origin block, whose captured membership is the EU-27 plus Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland, and the proposed place of landing comes from reference data's ports of entry endpoint, which is built and MDM-backed.
claims.quote: countries stay on GBNAG_SPS_EX, whose captured membership (EU-27 + IS, LI, NO, CH) covers every statutory origin, with the per-category narrowing in the set-owned commodities service (c-022)

claims.statement: There is no eligibility checker and no before-you-start page, and the dashboard's guidance link appears only while a real URL is set rather than as a placeholder link.
claims.quote: no eligibility or before-you-start page this run. The dashboard intro names the scheme and the three commodity groups and carries a GOV.UK guidance link only when guidanceUrl is set (never a # link)

claims.statement: The journey never asks which authority the notification goes to and shows no copy saying it has been sent anywhere, collecting only the commodity type and place of destination that routing would need.
claims.quote: the journey collects commodityType and placeOfDestination only, never asks which authority applies and shows no routing copy

claims.statement: There is no bulk upload: no file, template or upload page appears anywhere, and if one is ever built it must produce the same answers and pass the same validation as the form.
claims.quote: No file, template or upload page appears in the spec.

claims.statement: The service cannot read consignment details out of an existing document: there is no upload and extract route.
claims.quote: Not built in this phase. NNS-UN-042 stays a parked convenience need.

claims.statement: A trader cannot reuse a previous notification: there is no Copy as new action and no notification-copied banner, and the prototype's templates pattern is not adopted.
claims.quote: the dashboard and CYA action sets omit Copy as new and the Notification copied banner until this is unparked

claims.statement: No agent party, agent sign-in, authorisation or importer-to-agent link is collected, and the declaration carries no third-party authority clause.
claims.quote: The signed-in Defra ID organisation is the notifier; no agent party, agent sign-in model, authorisation or importer-agent link is collected. The declaration carries no third-party authority clause (c-028).

claims.statement: There is no plant-operator registration step: signing in with Defra ID is the only thing a trader must do before notifying.
claims.quote: Defra ID sign-in is the only precondition (c-039).

claims.statement: This frontend holds no regulator screen, filter or report; what the regulator needs is collected as coded category, genus and country, a structured destination address, the arrival date and status, the late flag and a stable reference.
claims.quote: No regulator screen, filter or report in this frontend.

claims.statement: The service records no inspection outcome, no non-notified consignment and no risk level: inspector-side capture lives elsewhere.
claims.quote: No inspector-side capture in this frontend: no outcome recording, no non-notified-consignment record, no risk level.

claims.statement: There is no export or download feature; the journey's duty to analysts is met by storing coded, structured values and extraction is backend work.
claims.quote: No export or download feature in this frontend.

claims.statement: There is no admin or list-maintenance screen and no spot-check percentage anywhere in the journey; a policy change to a commodity, category, genus or origin list is a data change in the set's commodities service.
claims.quote: No admin or list-maintenance surface in this frontend, and spot-check percentages and risk classifications are not represented in the notifier journey.

claims.statement: The journey has no check booked step, appointment slot, inspection date or notice to the trader; the only trace of checks is the confirmation and destination copy saying a check may happen without prior notice.
claims.quote: No scheduling, appointment, 'check booked' step or notice to the trader in this frontend; the hand-off to scheduling systems is backend work.

claims.statement: The journey carries no documents collection, upload page, uploader route, virus-scan polling or document reference at all.
claims.quote: No documents collection, upload page, cdp-uploader route, virus-scan polling or document reference in this run.

claims.statement: Submitting a notification writes the record and nothing else: there is no outbox, no event publishing and no routing on to other systems, and the confirmation makes no promise about where the notification has gone.
claims.quote: No outbox, no GBN-AG or other event publishing, no PIMS routing in this run.

claims.statement: The plants notification list shows plants notifications only, with no by-type filter, no journey-type label on a card and no combined list, so a trader who imports both animals and plants uses two dashboards.
claims.quote: No cross-journey 'By type' filter, no 'Plants' card label, no combined list; the INS front door owns any cross-journey list later.

claims.statement: The journey's share of the management information is coded values for the commodity type, category, genus and ISO country of origin, and the record's created and submitted timestamps; it measures nothing itself and adds no question for reporting.
claims.quote: the journey owes metrics 1-3 coded values (commodityType, category, genus as input.values; countryOfOrigin as ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) and metric 6 two envelope timestamps (createdAt at create, submittedAt = dateOfNotification at submit); it measures nothing itself and adds no question for MI

claims.statement: The notification list's Date submitted row is empty against the real backend, because the backend's list projection carries no submitted date.
claims.quote: the plants backend list projection carries no submittedAt (NotificationView: referenceNumber, concurrencyToken, status, created), so real/marshal/list-item.js:32 hardcodes submittedAt null and the dashboard Date submitted row is empty in real mode
claims.note: The specification records this as a defect with a fix extra named dashboard-date-submitted-real-list.

claims.statement: Submission is synchronous: the confirmation page appears only once the record has been stored as submitted with its date of notification stamped server-side, a failed store re-renders the declaration with the recoverable error, and no queue, batch or optimistic confirmation may come between.
claims.quote: no queue, batch or optimistic step may be introduced between submit and the persisted record

claims.statement: Equal internal access for Defra policy, Scottish Government and the Forestry Commission is another product's job; this journey's only part in it is the confirmation naming all three authorities without preferring one.
claims.quote: its one touchpoint is the confirmation page naming all three competent authorities without preferring one

claims.statement: Accessibility is held at WCAG 2.2 AA per page by the automated checks and the Lighthouse floor, with no page allowed to narrow the rule list or lower the floor, while a manual WCAG 2.2 audit and the service's own accessibility statement are still owed.
claims.quote: no page increment may narrow the axe tag list or lower the 0.70 floor

claims.statement: GDS standards are met by the toolbox components, one thing per page, the error summary, the task list overview, check your answers, the confirmation panel and the Alpha phase banner, which stays until the programme changes phase.
claims.quote: the Alpha phase banner stays until the programme moves phase (mural: Alpha Phase Confirmed - Update as Required, file:blueprint)

claims.statement: Before any copy taken from live animals ships, it is swept for animal-specific wording, the known case being the country of origin error that says the animal.
claims.quote: the copy pass sweeps it for animal-specific nouns — the known instance is countryOfOrigin errorCopy (Select the country where the animal originates from)

claims.statement: The personal data on a notification is the nominated contact's name, address, telephone number and email copied from the address book, plus the consignor's name and address, and no page may add personal data the policy paper does not list.
claims.quote: contactAddress (the nominated contact's name, address, telephone number and email address copied inline from the address book — c-025), consignor name and address

claims.statement: No lawful basis, privacy notice or retention period has been settled, and the backend stamps an expiry on a notification only outside production, so how long a production record is kept is undefined.
claims.quote: the plants backend stamps expireAt = created + ttl days in non-production only and never in production (NotificationService.stampExpiry; NotificationAggregate.expireAt), so production retention is undefined

claims.statement: The trader signs in with Defra ID and sees only their own organisation's notifications; internal username and password access is another product's concern and nothing more is built here.
claims.quote: Defra ID OIDC sign-in in real mode, the stub session with auth still enforced in STUB_MODE, and organisation-scoped records stand as adopted under stub-mode-and-sign-in and dashboard-listing; nothing more is built.

claims.statement: Nothing in the journey may stop a trader submitting because of the time of day, and lateness is judged on the London calendar day so a submission at any hour is judged on the right day.
claims.quote: The SI windows are counted in days with no hour-of-day cut-off (reg 24A(1) at least two days before; reg 26(1) no later than four days after), so nothing in the journey may gate submission by time of day.

claims.statement: The first release is English only, with the page language set to English and no language toggle, even though the requirement for a Welsh service stands, and no Welsh is invented.
claims.quote: it ships English-only with html lang en so assistive technology reads the page correctly, and copyFor keeps resolving en

claims.statement: Every answer for which a source gives a list is stored as a code and rendered through a label function, and every other answer is free text with a maximum length.
claims.quote: coded where a source gives a list (commodityType, category, genus, countryOfOrigin, proposedPlaceOfLanding, arrivalStatus, notificationStatus — stored as codes, rendered via service labels), free text with a max length otherwise (c-011)

claims.statement: Validation covers required-ness, membership for coded values including the per-category origin narrowing, a real calendar date, an HH:MM time, a whole number of one or more for quantity, a reference pattern for the consignment number and maximum lengths elsewhere, with no format yet for the commodity code, the EPPO code or the three identification numbers.
claims.quote: required-ness per the SI mandate; membership for coded values including the per-category origin narrowing with its notification-view re-check; dateText for arrivalDate; a new HH:MM time factory for arrivalTime; requiredIntegerInRange min 1 for quantity; the animals consignment-number pattern; animals max lengths elsewhere

claims.statement: Every question must trace to the statutory matters or the policy paper's common data list and no change may add one that does not, with the consignment number the only optional question, labelled optional and never gating readiness.
claims.quote: every question must trace to annex:5/reg:24A(2), reg:26(2) or the paper's Common Data list (annex:6 — Name of person making entry, Contact number, Contact address, Contact email), and no increment may add one that does not

claims.statement: The requirement that the system be sustainable is recorded with no reading adopted, and nothing in the journey depends on it.
claims.quote: Parked for policy to define (environmental, financial or maintainability); the panel adopts no reading.

claims.statement: The wood scope conditions on bark, origin, height and form are carried in the category option labels, and the exclusion of preservative-treated wood is a hint with its exception for cut coniferous trees, so the journey asks no screening question and has no page telling a trader they need not notify.
claims.quote: guidance only — the five category value labels carry the bark, origin, height and form conditions and category.input.hintByCommodityType carries the preservative exclusion with its cut-coniferous-trees exception (c-007); fuller scope text belongs with guidance-before-you-start, outside the journey pages

claims.statement: The seed and ware potato split is made by the line's category, the origin narrowing is validation, and the trader is never asked to declare that potatoes were suspected of having been grown somewhere.
claims.quote: the seed/ware split is the per-line category; the origin narrowing is validation owned by origin-value-list-by-commodity

claims.statement: The previous notification scheme and the Northern Irish and Irish services can only refine wording and value lists later, never change what the notification collects, because the statutory list fixes that.
claims.quote: Annex 2 equals the SI matters, so the previous scheme cannot change WHAT is collected.

claims.statement: Because the policy paper is a draft, every list is data behind the commodities service, each timing window is a single named constant read by the lateness rule and any hint that quotes it, and the territory wording and authority names are copy, so a policy change is a data or copy change rather than a model change.
claims.quote: the timing windows POTATO_DAYS_BEFORE_ARRIVAL = 2 (reg 24A(1)) and PLANTS_WOOD_DAYS_AFTER_ARRIVAL = 4 (reg 26(1)) are exported from one module beside the arrival-details feature and are the only place a window is written

claims.statement: Checks are made without prior notice, so the journey holds no check booked step, appointment slot or inspection date, and a post-arrival trader may give a current location instead of the destination, which is why the arrival status and the destination are captured together.
claims.quote: Policy also notes a post-arrival notifier may give a current location instead of the destination, so a check may happen elsewhere than first notified — that is why arrivalStatus + placeOfDestination are captured together.

claims.statement: The name of the person making the entry is read as the name on the contact address the trader picked, rather than the signed-in user's own name.
claims.quote: 'Name of person making entry' (annex:6/common-data/item:1) is read in the first pass as the picked contact's name carried by contactAddress

claims.statement: A trader cannot type an EU consignor's name and address on the notification: the consignor must be added to the address book first and then picked, and the address book demands a phone number and email address the law does not.
claims.quote: First pass: picker only, same as animals — the trader adds the consignor in the INS address book first; the pick is copied onto the notification and Edit details changes that copy for this notification only (EUDPA-662).

claims.statement: A notification asks once, and must have, what the trader is importing, offered as three radios labelled Potatoes (seed or ware), Plants for planting and Wood and cut trees.
claims.quote:
"values": ["potatoes", "plants-for-planting", "wood-and-cut-trees"],
        "valueLabels": "Potatoes (seed or ware) | Plants for planting | Wood and cut trees"

claims.statement: Each commodity type option carries its timing rule as a hint: potatoes must be notified at least 2 days before the expected date of arrival, and plants and wood before arrival or no later than 4 days after it; choosing nothing gives the error Select what you are importing.
claims.quote: You must notify at least 2 days before the expected date of arrival. | You must notify before arrival, or no later than 4 days after the date of arrival. | You must notify before arrival, or no later than 4 days after the date of arrival.

claims.statement: A notification holds one or more commodity lines, at least one being required, each line carrying a category, genus, species, commodity code, quantity, potato variety, potato intended use, EPPO code, size of tree and phytosanitary treatments as its scope allows.
claims.quote:
"item": [
        "category",
        "genus",
        "species",
        "commodityCode",
        "quantity",
        "potatoVariety",
        "potatoIntendedUse",
        "eppoCode",
        "sizeOfTree",
        "phytosanitaryTreatments"
      ]

claims.statement: A line is identified by its position in the notification rather than by any lasting identifier, and one line covers one category with its genus or variety.
claims.quote: one line per category + genus/variety; the entry page reconciles by position (snapshot-local index), never by a durable id

claims.statement: Each line must say its category, chosen from nine values: seed potatoes, ware potatoes, plants for planting, trees for planting, conifer wood with bark or isolated bark, conifer wood without bark from Italy, France, Portugal or Spain, cut coniferous trees more than 3 metres high, and wood of sweet chestnut, ash or plane either keeping its natural round surface or in unprocessed chips.
claims.quote: Seed potatoes | Ware potatoes | Plants for planting | Trees for planting | Conifer wood with bark, or isolated bark of conifer | Conifer wood without bark (from Italy, France, Portugal or Spain) | Cut coniferous trees more than 3 metres high | Wood of sweet chestnut, ash or plane that keeps all or part of its natural round surface | Wood of sweet chestnut, ash or plane in chips not processed into pellets or briquettes

claims.statement: The categories a line may hold depend on the notification's commodity type: seed and ware potatoes for potatoes, plants for planting and trees for planting for plants, and the five wood values for wood and cut trees, and the page offers only those.
claims.quote: the page offers only the values for the chosen notification-level commodityType

claims.statement: A wood notification's category question is hinted that preservative-treated wood does not need to be notified unless it is cut coniferous trees more than 3 metres high, and the plants options are hinted to separate shrubs and cuttings from trees, whose height will be asked.
claims.quote: "wood-and-cut-trees": "Preservative-treated wood does not need to be notified, unless it is cut coniferous trees more than 3 metres high."

claims.statement: A plants for planting, trees for planting or hardwood line must name its genus, chosen by type-ahead from fifteen entries: Castanea, Cedrus, Coffea, Fraxinus, Lavandula, Nerium oleander, Olea europaea, Picea, Pinus, Platanus, Polygala myrtifolia, Prunus, Quercus, Salvia rosmarinus and Ulmus.
claims.quote: Castanea (sweet chestnut) | Cedrus (cedar) | Coffea (coffee) | Fraxinus (ash) | Lavandula (lavender) | Nerium oleander (oleander) | Olea europaea (olive) | Picea (spruce) | Pinus (pine) | Platanus (plane) | Polygala myrtifolia (myrtle-leaf milkwort) | Prunus (plums, cherry etc) | Quercus (oak) | Salvia rosmarinus (rosemary) | Ulmus (elm)

claims.statement: A hardwood line offers only Castanea, Fraxinus and Platanus, a conifer line is asked no genus at all, and the page never offers a genus it would then reject.
claims.quote: the commodity-details page renders only valuesByCategory[category] from the set-owned commodities service (three entries for hardwood-round-surface and hardwood-chips, fifteen otherwise) and POST validates against that same list; it never offers fifteen and rejects twelve (c-017)

claims.statement: A plants for planting or trees for planting line must give the species as free text of up to 58 characters, hinted with the example Quercus robur and to enter the name as it appears on the plant passport.
claims.quote: For example, Quercus robur. Enter the species name as it appears on the plant passport.

claims.statement: Every line except a potato one must give the commodity code, free text of up to 58 characters hinted as the code from the UK Trade Tariff with the example 0602 20 20 and no format check.
claims.quote: The commodity code for these goods from the UK Trade Tariff. For example, 0602 20 20.

claims.statement: Every line must give a quantity as a whole number of one or more, hinted as the number of plants, tubers, trees or units of wood, with no unit asked.
claims.quote: For example, 250. Give the number of plants, tubers, trees or units of wood as a whole number.

claims.statement: A quantity that is not a whole number greater than nought is refused with Enter a whole number greater than 0, and a missing one with Enter the quantity.
claims.quote: Enter the quantity | Enter a whole number greater than 0

claims.statement: A potato line must give its variety as free text of up to 58 characters, hinted with the example Maris Piper, so a consignment of several varieties is several lines.
claims.quote: Per line so a shipment of several varieties is several lines (c-012); the SI pairs variety with quantity, which is the shared quantity obligation.
