claims.statement: The engine supplies per-instance scope, per-path wipe of out-of-scope paths that still hold data, per-instance completeness with the group complete when its floor is met and every instance is complete, and dispatch coverage at depth where a member inherits its owning page from the nearest ancestor group, so a loop page declares only the group.
claims.quote: - **Per-instance scope.** Every in-scope field of every instance is projected into the controller-facing scope

claims.statement: A collection needs a hand-written loop controller because a repeating group has no uniform-widget projection, and the controller reads and writes only through the engine barrel, never touching the evaluator.
claims.quote: A collection needs a hand-written loop controller. A repeating group has no uniform-widget projection, so each loop owns its rows and copy. The controller reads facts from the engine barrel ([`src/server/app/engine/index.js`](../../../engine/index.js)) and writes through it — it never touches the evaluator directly.

claims.statement: The engine's collection view returns facts only, an index, path, entry and completeness per instance, with no links, labels or view models, so the controller builds its own rows over those facts.
claims.quote: `state.collectionView(answers, collectionPath, evaluation)` returns facts only: `[{ index, path, entry, complete }]`. No hrefs, no labels, no view-models. The controller builds its own rows over those facts.

claims.statement: In the commodity lines shape two pages are in the flow: a list page that declares the group, reads the collection view for its rows and removes an instance, and an entry sub-page that collects nothing of its own and appends or updates exactly one instance.
claims.quote: Two pages the flow knows about: a LIST page that declares the group in `collects`, reads `collectionView` for its rows and removes an instance, and an ENTRY SUB-PAGE that collects nothing of its own (`collects: []`) and appends or updates exactly one instance.

claims.statement: The commodity entry sub-page carries the index it is editing rather than reconciling a selection, and an index the collection has no entry for is refused rather than acted on.
claims.quote: The sub-page carries the index it is editing rather than reconciling a selection, so nothing here uses `reconcileEntriesAt` and no page edits every line at once.

claims.statement: In a single-page loop the POST branches on the submit button: an add validates the entry fields and appends, a plain Continue advances with no write, and the append is what creates the snapshot-local position, so until that POST the draft lives only in the payload and never as a half-created instance in the store.
claims.quote: Its POST branches on the submit button. `action === 'add'` validates the entry fields and appends; a plain Continue advances with no write. The append creates the snapshot-local position — until that POST the draft lives only in the payload, never a half-created instance in the store:

claims.statement: An entry with no bound leaf has no canonical record to infer an instance from and is not persisted, so a collection form commits an entry only after validation has produced at least one bound leaf.
claims.quote: A leaf-less entry has no canonical record from which to infer an instance and is therefore not persisted. Collection forms should commit an entry only after validation has produced at least one bound leaf.

claims.statement: Remove is a third branch of the same POST, a submit button carrying the index, so the page form's crumb travels with it and no GET can trigger a delete, and the remove splices the instance out and reconciles so anything left dangling out of scope is pruned too.
claims.quote: Remove is a third branch of the same POST — a submit button named `action` with a `remove:<index>` value, so the page form's crumb travels with it and no GET can trigger a delete. It splices the instance out and reconciles, so anything left dangling out of scope is pruned too:

claims.statement: A loop looks the instance up before writing and refuses an index the collection has no entry for, so a forged or stale index is rejected rather than acted on.
claims.quote: Look the instance up before writing and refuse an index the collection has no entry for, so a forged or stale index is rejected rather than acted on.
claims.note: Stated as a write guard; named in general terms only.

claims.statement: The top-level append, update and remove operations are convenience forms that each delegate to the path form with a single-segment path.
claims.quote: `appendEntry` / `updateEntry` / `removeEntry` are the top-level convenience forms; each delegates to the `…At` form with a single-segment path

claims.statement: In a batch split the search page declares the group and on save reconciles one line per selected item in a single write, keeping a still-selected line's data including its nested records and dropping a deselected line with wipe semantics, while the consolidated details page collects nothing, renders the selected lines with a per-line Remove and an Add-another link, and edits every line in place.
claims.quote: `reconcileEntriesAt` keys existing instances by `keyOf`, keeps a still-selected line's data (including its nested records), and drops a deselected line with wipe semantics. The CONSOLIDATED DETAILS page collects nothing (`collects: []`), renders the selected lines with a per-line Remove and an Add-another link, and edits every line in place

claims.statement: A nested collection lives one card per parent line, appending and removing on a path that names the parent index, and reads its instances with the same collection view one level deeper.
claims.quote: A collection one level down lives one card per commodity line. It appends and removes on a two-segment-plus-index path:

claims.statement: A collection page carries where the trader came from whether it was reached from a review Change link, the Overview, the dashboard or the page before it, and every internal link and redirect, including row actions, Back, add, remove and save round trips, carries the trail so it survives the loop.
claims.quote: A collection page carries where the trader came from, whether it was reached from a Change link on check-your-answers, the Overview, the dashboard or the page before it. Wrap every internal link and redirect (row actions, Back, add, remove and save round trips) in `kit.carryTrail(request, href)` so the trail survives the loop.

claims.statement: Every mid-loop action keeps the trader in the loop on the page, and the loop moves on only from its exiting Continue, which goes to the next page in the journey's one page order and adds the collection page to the trail, while Save and return to overview goes to the Overview because a hub exit wins first.
claims.quote: Every mid-loop action keeps the trader in the loop, on the page. The loop moves on only from its exiting Continue, which goes to the next page in the journey's one page order through `kit.nextTarget(request, page, scope)`, adding the collection page to the trail. Save and return to overview goes to the Overview: a hub exit wins first via `kit.hubExitTarget(request)`.

claims.statement: A declared cap reads the named sibling count field in the frame that holds the collection and returns no cap when none is declared, the count is unanswered, or the value is not a non-negative integer; an unanswered count is deliberately no cap, because the per-instance floor still bites at submit so a blank count never lets a journey finish early.
claims.quote: `collectionCapAt` reads the named sibling in the frame that holds the collection and returns the cap, or `null` when there is no cap declared, the count is unanswered, or the value is not a non-negative integer. An **unanswered count is deliberately no cap** — the per-instance floor still bites at submit, so a blank count never lets a journey finish early.

claims.statement: Cap enforcement lives on the write path: the append reads the cap and makes no write when the list is already at it, so a stale form racing the cap is rejected rather than silently over-filling.
claims.quote: Enforcement lives on the write path: `appendEntryAt` reads the cap and returns `null` (no write) when the list is already at it, so a stale form racing the cap is rejected rather than silently over-filling.

claims.statement: The cap map is empty, an entry is added when the first capped collection lands, and an entry naming obligations the set does not declare is inert.
claims.quote: `MAX_ENTRIES_FROM` is empty. Add an entry mapping the collection name to its sibling count field when the first capped collection lands; an entry naming obligations this set does not declare is inert.

claims.statement: A nested loop's remove handler must validate the parent index before touching the store, because the write primitives act at whatever path they are given and an out-of-range parent index would fabricate a phantom parent instance.
claims.quote: **Validate the parent index in a nested loop.** The write primitives append or splice at whatever path you give them. An out-of-range parent index would fabricate a phantom parent instance.
claims.note: A write guard the docs say must not be removed; named in general terms only.

claims.statement: The engine rejects a non-integer collection index, because a malformed index would otherwise be coerced into removing the first instance.
claims.quote: **The engine rejects non-integer indices.** `isValidIndex` in [`src/server/app/engine/write/pipeline/predicates.js`](../../../engine/write/pipeline/predicates.js) uses `Number.isInteger` because `splice(NaN, 1)` coerces to `splice(0, 1)` — a malformed remove URL would otherwise destroy the first instance.
claims.note: A write guard the docs say must not be removed; named in general terms only.
